title: UK Postcode Distance Calculator
description: The UK Postcode Distance Calculator gives the straight-line distance between any two UK postcodes in km and miles, from postcodes.io data. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, SW1A 1AA in Westminster to M1 1AE in Manchester measures approx. 262.0 km (162.8 miles) in a straight line — the drive is longer, because the motorway network cannot follow the geometric minimum.
quick_answer: The UK Postcode Distance Calculator measures the straight-line distance between any two UK postcodes. Enter both postcodes and it looks up their coordinates from postcodes.io, applies the haversine formula, and shows the result in kilometres and miles — the fast way to compare two addresses anywhere in the UK.
steps_intro: Two postcodes, one honest number — useful whenever a form, a quote or a territory decision depends on how far apart two UK addresses really are:

body.t: Many UK trades price by distance from base. A straight-line figure between your postcode and the customer's is the consistent first pass for a call-out band — then check the actual journey in the
or a driving tool before quoting a time.
Agencies matching staff to clients need to know which carer or engineer is genuinely nearest. Postcode-to-postcode distance beats guessing from town names, especially where two towns share a border.
Comparing a new home against the office, a school or family is a distance question before it is a viewing. Run the candidate postcodes here, then test the realistic journey time separately.

Students and analysts joining UK datasets use postcode distance to validate records and spot the row where a digit was transposed — a London postcode suddenly 400 km from its neighbours announces the error.

SW1A 1AA (Westminster) to EH1 1YZ (Edinburgh) computes to approx. 533.9 km (331.8 miles) in a straight line. The rail and road journeys are both longer — the number here is the geographic fact underneath them, and the right baseline for comparing the same trip against Glasgow or Cardiff.

Scotland's two cities are close enough that the method matters: EH1 1YZ to G1 1AA is approx. 66.8 km (41.5 miles) as the crow flies. Two postcodes in the same city can differ by several kilometres, which is why the calculator takes the full postcode rather than the district alone.

popular_table.title: Popular UK postcode pairs
popular_table.intro: Straight-line distances between well-known UK postcodes, computed with this tool's method — coordinates from postcodes.io, haversine on the mean sphere — and rounded; treat as approx. planning figures, not road mileage.
popular_table.note: Distances run between postcode centroids — the representative point postcodes.io publishes for each code. Two addresses sharing a postcode can still be a short walk apart.

faq: Do I need the full postcode, or is the district enough?

Use the full postcode (for example SW1A 1AA, not just SW1A). The distance is measured between the coordinates postcodes.io publishes for the complete code; a district covers a wide area and would make the answer depend on which point in it you happened to pick.

No — it is the straight-line (great-circle) distance between the two postcode coordinates. Road distance is always longer because roads follow the network. Use this figure for consistent comparisons and charge bands, and a routing tool for the actual journey.
Where do the coordinates come from?

From postcodes.io, the open UK postcode dataset built on Ordnance Survey and ONS data. Each postcode resolves to a representative latitude and longitude, which is what the haversine calculation consumes.
Does it work for Northern Ireland?
Yes — BT postcodes are part of the same postcodes.io dataset, so Belfast to London computes the same way as any mainland pair (approx. 517.6 km, 321.6 miles, in a straight line across the Irish Sea).
Why does my result differ from a mileage calculator?

Because they measure different things. Mileage follows roads; this tool measures geometry. The gap between the two grows where roads must detour around water, hills or sparse networks — the comparison itself is often the useful insight.
How accurate is a postcode-to-postcode distance?

As accurate as the postcode centroids: for most urban codes that is within a few hundred metres of the address, and rural codes cover larger areas. It is a planning and comparison figure, not a surveyed measurement between two front doors.
Can I compare many postcodes at once?
This page answers one pair at a time, carefully. For a table of every pair among several places, extract the coordinates and use the Distance Matrix Calculator.
